# Overview

ChAMP2 performs the complete analysis of Illumina Infinium methylation arrays:
loading, filtering, quality control, normalisation, batch correction,
differential methylation at the probe (DMP) and region (DMR, block) level,
copy-number analysis, cell-type correction and gene-set enrichment.

This release (2.32.0) is a compatibility rewrite: **one source tree runs on
R 4.2.3 through 4.6.2** (Bioconductor 3.16 through 3.24). The algorithms that
ChAMP used to import from packages which are no longer installable everywhere
(`impute`, `RPMM`, `kpmt`, and the DMRcate backend) are now bundled, and every
optional feature tells you exactly which package it needs.

# Installation

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# 1. install every dependency for the running R/Bioconductor version
Rscript inst/scripts/install_deps.R      # or: ChAMP::champ_install_deps()

# 2. install ChAMP
# R CMD INSTALL ChAMP2
```

After loading the package, `champ_check_env()` prints which optional features
are available:

```{r checkenv, eval=FALSE}
library(ChAMP)
champ_check_env()
```

# A complete run in one call

`champ.process()` chains every step and stores the results of each one:

```{r process, eval=FALSE}
myResults <- champ.process(
    directory   = "IDAT/",
    arraytype   = "EPICv2",     # "450K", "EPICv1" or "EPICv2"
    DMRmethod   = "Bumphunter",
    resultsDir  = "./CHAMP_RESULT/",
    cores       = 4)
names(myResults)
```

The rest of this vignette runs the same steps one at a time, which is the
recommended approach: it is easier to inspect intermediate objects and to
re-run a single step.

# Loading data

Two back-ends are available:

* `method = "ChAMP"` (default) reads the IDAT files directly using the ChAMP
  annotation. It does not need minfi and works for 450K, EPICv1 and EPICv2.
* `method = "minfi"` uses `minfi::read.metharray.exp()`. It is required if you
  want SWAN or FunctionalNormalization later, because those need the
  `RGChannelSet`.

```{r load, eval=FALSE}
myLoad <- champ.load(
    directory    = "IDAT/",
    arraytype    = "450K",
    method       = "ChAMP",
    filterXY     = TRUE,
    filterSNPs   = TRUE,
    filterMultiHit = TRUE,
    filterBeads  = TRUE,
    filterNoCG   = TRUE,
    detPcut      = 0.01,
    SampleCutoff = 0.1)

names(myLoad)       # beta, pd, intensity, detP
dim(myLoad$beta)
```

Rows with failed probes can be filtered and imputed later with
`champ.impute()`; `champ.filter()` exposes the same filtering engine for data
that was loaded elsewhere.

# Quality control

```{r qc, eval=FALSE}
champ.QC(beta       = myLoad$beta,
         pheno      = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
         mdsPlot     = TRUE,
         densityPlot = TRUE,
         dendrogram  = TRUE,
         resultsDir  = "./CHAMP_QCimages/")
```

The three plots are implemented in ChAMP itself, so QC works even when minfi
is not installed.

# Normalisation

`BMIQ` is the default and only needs the beta matrix and the probe design
type, which is read from the annotation. `PBC` is a fast alternative; `SWAN`
and `FunctionalNormalization` need the `RGChannelSet` from `method = "minfi"`.

```{r norm, eval=FALSE}
myNorm <- champ.norm(beta       = myLoad$beta,
                     rgSet      = myLoad$rgSet,
                     mset       = myLoad$mset,
                     method     = "BMIQ",
                     arraytype  = "450K",
                     cores      = 4,
                     resultsDir = "./CHAMP_Normalization/")
```

BMIQ's beta-mixture step uses `champ_blc()`, a bundled implementation of the
`RPMM::blc()` model. If RPMM is installed it is used instead, so results are
unchanged for existing users.

# Batch effects

`champ.SVD()` tests every factor of the sample sheet against the top singular
vectors; `champ.runCombat()` then corrects the batch variables you name while
keeping the phenotype in the model.

```{r svd, eval=FALSE}
champ.SVD(beta  = myNorm,
          rgSet = myLoad$rgSet,
          pd    = myLoad$pd,
          resultsDir = "./CHAMP_SVDimages/")

myCombat <- champ.runCombat(beta     = myNorm,
                            pd       = myLoad$pd,
                            variablename = "Sample_Group",
                            batchname    = c("Slide"))
```

# Differential methylation

## Probes (DMP)

```{r dmp, eval=FALSE}
myDMP <- champ.DMP(beta   = myCombat,
                    pheno  = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                    adjPVal = 0.05,
                    adjust.method = "BH")
head(myDMP[[1]])
```

A numeric phenotype (age, for example) is analysed by linear regression and the
result is stored under `"NumericVariable"`. With more than two groups every pair
is compared unless `compare.group` is given.

## Regions (DMR)

```{r dmr, eval=FALSE}
myDMR <- champ.DMR(beta   = myCombat,
                   pheno  = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                   method = "Bumphunter",
                   minProbes = 7,
                   adjPvalDmr = 0.05,
                   cores = 4)
```

`method` may also be `"ProbeLasso"` or `"DMRcate"`. The DMRcate method uses the
DMRcate package when it is installed and otherwise the identical algorithm in
`champ_dmrcate()`; set `dmrcate.backend = "internal"` to always use the bundled
version (no ExperimentHub download, works for EPICv2).

## Blocks

```{r block, eval=FALSE}
myBlock <- champ.Block(beta  = myCombat,
                       pheno = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                       arraytype = "450K")
```

# Gene-set enrichment

```{r gsea, eval=FALSE}
myGSEA <- champ.GSEA(beta = myCombat,
                     DMP  = myDMP[[1]],
                     DMR  = myDMR,
                     arraytype = "450K",
                     method = "fisher")

myEbGSEA <- champ.ebGSEA(beta = myCombat,
                         pheno = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                         arraytype = "450K")
```

`champ.GSEA()` also supports `method = "goseq"` (needs goseq and
geneLenDataBase) and `method = "gometh"` (needs missMethyl). The `P(KPMT)`
column comes from `champ_kpmt()`, an exact implementation of the
known-population median test.

# Copy number and cell composition

```{r cna, eval=FALSE}
myCNA <- champ.CNA(intensity = myLoad$intensity,
                   pheno     = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group,
                   arraytype = "450K")

myRefbase <- champ.refbase(beta = myCombat, arraytype = "450K")
```

# Interactive exploration

```{r gui, eval=FALSE}
DMP.GUI(myDMP[[1]], beta = myCombat, pheno = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group)
DMR.GUI(myDMR[[1]], beta = myCombat, pheno = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group)
QC.GUI(beta = myCombat, pheno = myLoad$pd$Sample_Group)
```

Pass `runApp = FALSE` to obtain the Shiny app object without launching it.

# A small self-contained example

The chunk below does not need any IDAT files: it builds a synthetic beta matrix
on real 450K probe identifiers and runs the parts of the pipeline that only need
a matrix.

```{r demo, eval=requireNamespace("ChAMPdata", quietly = TRUE)}
library(ChAMP)
pf <- ChAMP:::.champ_probe_features("450K")
ids <- rownames(pf)[!is.na(pf$MAPINFO)][1:2000]
set.seed(1)
beta <- matrix(rbeta(length(ids) * 10, 2, 5), nrow = length(ids),
               dimnames = list(ids, paste0("S", 1:10)))
group <- rep(c("Control", "Case"), each = 5)
beta[1:80, group == "Case"] <- pmin(1 - 1e-6, beta[1:80, group == "Case"] + 0.3)

norm <- champ.norm(beta, method = "PBC", arraytype = "450K", verbose = FALSE,
                   resultsDir = tempfile("norm"))
dmp  <- champ.DMP(norm, pheno = group, arraytype = "450K", verbose = FALSE)
head(dmp[[1]][, c("logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val", "gene")], 3)
```
